## Objetivo de negocio

Los pronósticos horarios ayudan a posicionar bicicletas antes de los picos. Este notebook muestra el flujo completo: validación, tipado de variables, partición temporal, preprocesamiento, ajuste, métricas finales, importancia y diagnóstico de residuos.

## Cargar paquetes


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(readr)
library(tibble)
library(tidymodels)
library(tidyr)
```
:::


## Leer y validar el snapshot


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
bikes <- read_csv(
  here("data", "seoul_bike_snapshot.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  col_types = cols(date = col_date())
) |>
  mutate(
    weekday = factor(weekday),
    season = factor(season),
    holiday = factor(holiday),
    functioning_day = factor(functioning_day),
    is_weekend = factor(is_weekend)
  ) |>
  arrange(date, hour)

required_columns <- c(
  "date", "rented_bike_count", "hour", "temperature_c",
  "humidity_pct", "wind_speed_ms", "visibility_10m",
  "dew_point_c", "solar_radiation_mj_m2", "rainfall_mm",
  "snowfall_cm", "season", "holiday", "functioning_day",
  "weekday", "is_weekend"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, names(bikes))

if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Faltan columnas de bicicletas: ",
    paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

stopifnot(
  !any(bikes$rented_bike_count < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  anyDuplicated(bikes[c("date", "hour")]) == 0,
  all(bikes$hour %in% 0:23)
)

bikes |>
  summarise(
    observaciones = n(),
    primera_fecha = min(date),
    ultima_fecha = max(date),
    alquiler_promedio = mean(rented_bike_count),
    alquiler_maximo = max(rented_bike_count)
  ) |>
  kable(digits = 1)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


| observaciones|primera_fecha |ultima_fecha | alquiler_promedio| alquiler_maximo|
|-------------:|:-------------|:------------|-----------------:|---------------:|
|          8760|2017-12-01    |2018-11-30   |             704.6|            3556|


:::
:::


## Análisis exploratorio

La variable objetivo conserva unidades reales. Su distribución asimétrica muestra que las horas de demanda alta son menos frecuentes, pero importantes para la operación.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(bikes, aes(x = rented_bike_count)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 40,
    fill = "#2A9D8F",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "La demanda horaria está sesgada hacia la derecha",
    x = "Bicicletas alquiladas",
    y = "Horas"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/rental-distribution-1.png){fig-alt='Histograma del número horario de bicicletas alquiladas.' width=672}
:::
:::


Los promedios diarios exponen la estacionalidad y los periodos sin operación.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
daily_demand <- bikes |>
  group_by(date) |>
  summarise(
    average_demand = mean(rented_bike_count),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(daily_demand, aes(x = date, y = average_demand)) +
  geom_line(color = "#457B9D", alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_smooth(
    se = FALSE,
    color = "#E76F51",
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "La demanda diaria cambia durante el año",
    x = "Fecha",
    y = "Bicicletas alquiladas en promedio"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/daily-demand-1.png){fig-alt='Demanda diaria promedio durante el periodo observado.' width=672}
:::
:::


Las dispersiones muestreadas permiten observar relaciones meteorológicas no lineales antes de introducir el random forest.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
weather_relationships <- bikes |>
  filter(functioning_day == "Yes") |>
  slice(seq(1, n(), by = 4)) |>
  select(
    rented_bike_count,
    temperature_c,
    humidity_pct,
    solar_radiation_mj_m2,
    rainfall_mm
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -rented_bike_count,
    names_to = "predictor",
    values_to = "value"
  )

ggplot(
  weather_relationships,
  aes(x = value, y = rented_bike_count)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, color = "#457B9D") +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "#E76F51") +
  facet_wrap(
    vars(predictor),
    scales = "free_x",
    ncol = 2
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Las relaciones meteorológicas son no lineales",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Bicicletas alquiladas"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

## Demanda por hora y estación


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
hourly_demand <- bikes |>

```

## Definir datos sin fuga de información

Los cierres se excluyen porque sus ceros representan servicio no disponible. Se eliminan la fecha cruda y el indicador redundante de fin de semana; se conserva el día de la semana.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
modeling_data <- bikes |>
  filter(functioning_day == "Yes") |>
  select(-functioning_day, -is_weekend)

set.seed(2026)

bike_split <- initial_time_split(modeling_data, prop = 0.8)
training_data <- training(bike_split)
testing_data <- testing(bike_split)
resamples <- vfold_cv(training_data, v = 3)

tibble(
  particion = c("Entrenamiento y ajuste", "Prueba final"),
  observaciones = c(nrow(training_data), nrow(testing_data)),
  primera_fecha = c(min(training_data$date), min(testing_data$date)),
  ultima_fecha = c(max(training_data$date), max(testing_data$date))
) |>
  kable()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|particion              | observaciones|primera_fecha |ultima_fecha |
|:----------------------|-------------:|:-------------|:------------|
|Entrenamiento y ajuste |          6772|2017-12-01    |2018-09-11   |
|Prueba final           |          1693|2018-09-11    |2018-11-30   |


:::
:::


## Línea base de la media


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
baseline_predictions <- testing_data |>
  transmute(
    rented_bike_count,
    .pred = mean(training_data$rented_bike_count)
  )
```
:::


## Receta de preprocesamiento

La fecha no entra en la fórmula. Los niveles categóricos se tratan antes de crear indicadores, se eliminan columnas sin variación y la normalización se estima solo en cada fold.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
bike_recipe <- recipe(
  rented_bike_count ~
    hour +
    temperature_c +
    humidity_pct +
    wind_speed_ms +
    visibility_10m +
    dew_point_c +
    solar_radiation_mj_m2 +
    rainfall_mm +
    snowfall_cm +
    season +
    holiday +
    weekday,
  data = training_data
) |>
  step_unknown(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = FALSE) |>
  step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())
```
:::


## Regresión lineal


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
linear_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(bike_recipe) |>
  add_model(
    linear_reg() |>
      set_engine("lm")
  )

linear_fit <- fit(linear_workflow, data = training_data)

linear_predictions <- bind_cols(
  testing_data |> select(rented_bike_count),
  predict(linear_fit, new_data = testing_data)
)
```
:::


## Elastic Net


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
elastic_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(bike_recipe) |>
  add_model(
    linear_reg(
      penalty = tune(),
      mixture = tune()
    ) |>
      set_engine("glmnet")
  )

elastic_grid <- grid_space_filling(
  penalty(range = c(-5, 1)),
  mixture(),
  size = 6
)

elastic_results <- tune_grid(
  elastic_workflow,
  resamples = resamples,
  grid = elastic_grid,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae, rsq_trad)
)

best_elastic <- select_best(elastic_results, metric = "rmse")
best_elastic |> kable(digits = 5)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


| penalty| mixture|.config         |
|-------:|-------:|:---------------|
| 0.00016|       1|pre0_mod2_post0 |


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
elastic_fit <- elastic_workflow |>
  finalize_workflow(best_elastic) |>
  fit(data = training_data)

elastic_predictions <- bind_cols(
  testing_data |> select(rented_bike_count),
  predict(elastic_fit, new_data = testing_data)
)
```
:::


## Random forest


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
forest_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(bike_recipe) |>
  add_model(
    rand_forest(
      mtry = tune(),
      min_n = tune(),
      trees = 300
    ) |>
      set_engine("ranger", importance = "permutation") |>
      set_mode("regression")
  )

forest_grid <- grid_space_filling(
  mtry(range = c(3L, 12L)),
  min_n(range = c(5L, 35L)),
  size = 6
)

forest_results <- tune_grid(
  forest_workflow,
  resamples = resamples,
  grid = forest_grid,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae, rsq_trad)
)

best_forest <- select_best(forest_results, metric = "rmse")
best_forest |> kable()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


| mtry| min_n|.config         |
|----:|-----:|:---------------|
|   10|    11|pre0_mod5_post0 |


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
forest_fit <- forest_workflow |>
  finalize_workflow(best_forest) |>
  fit(data = training_data)

forest_predictions <- bind_cols(
  testing_data |> select(rented_bike_count),
  predict(forest_fit, new_data = testing_data)
)
```
:::


La superficie de ajuste muestra cómo la complejidad de los árboles y el tamaño mínimo de nodo afectan el error de validación.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
forest_tuning <- forest_results |>
  collect_metrics() |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse")

ggplot(
  forest_tuning,
  aes(
    x = mtry,
    y = min_n,
    color = mean,
    size = mean
  )
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(
    option = "C",
    direction = -1
  ) +
  scale_size(
    range = c(3, 7),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Superficie de ajuste del random forest",
    subtitle = "Un RMSE menor indica mejor resultado de validación",
    x = "Predictores evaluados por división (mtry)",
    y = "Observaciones mínimas por nodo",
    color = "RMSE"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/forest-tuning-1.png){fig-alt='Combinaciones de ajuste del random forest coloreadas por RMSE de validación.' width=672}
:::
:::


## Rendimiento en la prueba final


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
baseline_metrics <- bind_rows(
  rmse(baseline_predictions, rented_bike_count, .pred),
  mae(baseline_predictions, rented_bike_count, .pred),
  rsq_trad(baseline_predictions, rented_bike_count, .pred)
) |>
  mutate(model = "Línea base")

linear_metrics <- bind_rows(
  rmse(linear_predictions, rented_bike_count, .pred),
  mae(linear_predictions, rented_bike_count, .pred),
  rsq_trad(linear_predictions, rented_bike_count, .pred)
) |>
  mutate(model = "Regresión lineal")

elastic_metrics <- bind_rows(
  rmse(elastic_predictions, rented_bike_count, .pred),
  mae(elastic_predictions, rented_bike_count, .pred),
  rsq_trad(elastic_predictions, rented_bike_count, .pred)
) |>
  mutate(model = "Elastic Net")

forest_metrics <- bind_rows(
  rmse(forest_predictions, rented_bike_count, .pred),
  mae(forest_predictions, rented_bike_count, .pred),
  rsq_trad(forest_predictions, rented_bike_count, .pred)
) |>
  mutate(model = "Random forest")

holdout_metrics <- bind_rows(
  baseline_metrics,
  linear_metrics,
  elastic_metrics,
  forest_metrics
) |>
  select(model, .metric, .estimate)

metrics_table <- holdout_metrics |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = .metric,
    values_from = .estimate
  ) |>
  arrange(rmse)

metrics_table |>
  kable(digits = 2)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|model            |   rmse|    mae| rsq_trad|
|:----------------|------:|------:|--------:|
|Random forest    | 348.17| 246.34|     0.66|
|Regresión lineal | 432.95| 319.56|     0.48|
|Elastic Net      | 433.05| 317.66|     0.48|
|Línea base       | 634.41| 491.51|    -0.12|


:::
:::


RMSE y MAE se mantienen interpretables como bicicletas alquiladas.

## Observado frente a predicho


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
prediction_comparison <- bind_rows(
  baseline_predictions |>
    mutate(model = "Línea base"),
  linear_predictions |>
    mutate(model = "Regresión lineal"),
  elastic_predictions |>
    mutate(model = "Elastic Net"),
  forest_predictions |>
    mutate(model = "Random forest")
) |>
  mutate(
    model = factor(
      model,
      levels = c(
        "Línea base",
        "Regresión lineal",
        "Elastic Net",
        "Random forest"
      )
    )
  )

ggplot(
  prediction_comparison,
  aes(x = rented_bike_count, y = .pred)
) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = 1,
    intercept = 0,
    color = "#E76F51",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, color = "#2A9D8F") +
  facet_wrap(vars(model), ncol = 2) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "Demanda observada y predicha en horas futuras no vistas",
    x = "Bicicletas observadas",
    y = "Bicicletas predichas"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/observed-predicted-1.png){fig-alt='Gráficos facetados de valores observados y predichos para cuatro modelos.' width=672}
:::
:::


## Importancia de variables


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
forest_engine <- extract_fit_engine(forest_fit)

variable_importance <- enframe(
  forest_engine$variable.importance,
  name = "variable",
  value = "importance"
) |>
  arrange(desc(importance)) |>
  slice_head(n = 12)
```
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(
  variable_importance,
  aes(x = importance, y = reorder(variable, importance))
) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2A9D8F") +
  labs(
    title = "Importancia por permutación del random forest",
    x = "Importancia",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/variable-importance-chart-1.png){fig-alt='Barras horizontales con las variables más importantes del random forest.' width=672}
:::
:::


## Diagnóstico de residuos


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
forest_diagnostics <- forest_predictions |>
  mutate(residual = rented_bike_count - .pred)

ggplot(forest_diagnostics, aes(x = .pred, y = residual)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#555555") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35, color = "#2A9D8F") +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "#E76F51") +
  labs(
    title = "Residuos del random forest en observaciones no vistas",
    x = "Bicicletas predichas",
    y = "Observado menos predicho"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/residual-chart-1.png){fig-alt='Residuos frente a predicciones del random forest en la prueba final.' width=672}
:::
:::


## Conclusión

- El random forest es el mejor modelo final, con RMSE de 348.17, MAE de 246.34 y R² de 0.66.
- Frente a la línea base reduce el RMSE en 45.1% y el MAE en 49.9%.
- El bosque seleccionado utiliza un valor `mtry` de 10 y un valor `min_n` de 11; Elastic Net se comporta como lasso (`mixture` = 1) con penalización 1.58e-04.
- Las variables líderes por importancia de permutación son hour, temperature_c, solar_radiation_mj_m2, humidity_pct, dew_point_c, lo que confirma que la hora y los efectos meteorológicos no lineales concentran la capacidad predictiva.
- La dispersión de residuos aumenta en periodos de alta demanda. El modelo funciona como referencia para planeación urbana, pero necesita calibración de picos, reentrenamiento continuo y variables por estación para uso operativo.

Consulta la [versión en inglés](../index.qmd).
